feature.title: Employee onboarding questionnaire
feature.goal: A new employee answers one short, conditional English questionnaire once, and Lonio records exactly the data that Pensionskasse Muster, source tax (the Zurich tariff) and Muster AG HR need for that person. From the answers it derives the insurance start date and the full source tax tariff code, and it collects no personal data that no party needs.

sections.title: Personal details and home address
sections.purpose: Collect the employee's name, date of birth and complete postal address, which also gives the country of residence, and the canton for Swiss residents, so the fund can register the employee and HR can post documents.

stories.title: Personal details for the pension fund registration
stories.i_want: every new employee to give their first name, last name and date of birth
stories.so_that: the employee can be registered as an insured person; the registration is rejected if any of these required fields is missing
stories.priority_reason: The fund's registration form marks these fields as required and refuses the registration while they are empty, so missing data blocks the registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: Name and date of birth are always asked and required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee starts the questionnaire, wherever they live
acceptance_criteria.when: they fill in the first step, personal details
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for their first name, last name and date of birth, and they cannot submit the questionnaire while any of the three is empty

acceptance_criteria.title: Date of birth is a full calendar date
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is asked for their date of birth
acceptance_criteria.when: they enter it
acceptance_criteria.then: it is recorded as day, month and year (DD.MM.YYYY), as the pension fund expects it

acceptance_criteria.title: Personal details are recorded for the pension fund
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: the answers are recorded
acceptance_criteria.then: first name, last name and date of birth are recorded as needed for the pension fund registration, each asked only once

stories.title: Complete home address for posting documents
stories.i_want: every new employee to give their complete home address: street, house number, postcode, town and country
stories.so_that: HR can post documents to the employee without missing address parts
stories.priority_reason: HR posts many documents to employees and explicitly states the address must be complete.

acceptance_criteria.title: All five address parts are always asked and required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee is in the second step, home address
acceptance_criteria.when: they fill in their address
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for street, house number, postcode, town and country, and cannot submit the questionnaire while any of them is empty

acceptance_criteria.title: Address as written on an envelope, nothing more
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee enters their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: the address is asked
acceptance_criteria.then: only a normal postal address is asked, as one would write it on an envelope, with the country given by its English name (e.g. "Switzerland", "Germany"); no further address details are asked

acceptance_criteria.title: Address is recorded for HR
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: the answers are recorded
acceptance_criteria.then: the complete home address is recorded for HR to post documents

stories.title: Home address country is the country of residence for later questions
stories.i_want: the country of the home address to be used as the employee's country of residence, without asking it again
stories.so_that: living abroad, and which cross-border questions apply, follow from one answer, and the employee is not asked the same thing twice
stories.priority_reason: Living abroad makes the employee subject to source tax regardless of nationality; a wrong or missing residence leads to a wrong source tax decision.

acceptance_criteria.title: Residence is not asked a second time
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: later steps need to know where the employee lives (main residence in Switzerland, state of residence)
acceptance_criteria.then: the home address country is used as the country of residence and the employee is not asked for their residence again

acceptance_criteria.title: Living abroad makes the employee subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: the home address country is not Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire decides which questions follow
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee counts as living abroad and is subject to source tax whatever their nationality, so nationality and the canton are not asked; an employee living in Switzerland is asked for nationality and canton

stories.title: Canton of residence for employees living in Switzerland
stories.i_want: employees living in Switzerland to choose their canton from the 26 Swiss cantons
stories.so_that: the required 'Canton' field of the registration can be filled, while employees abroad are not asked for a canton they do not have
stories.priority_reason: 'Canton' is a required field at the fund; without it the registration is refused.

acceptance_criteria.title: Canton asked and required only from residents of Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: the home address step is completed
acceptance_criteria.then: an employee living in Switzerland is asked for the canton and cannot submit without it; an employee living abroad is not asked. This is provisional: what the fund needs for employees abroad, and whether 'Canton' means residence or work, is open (see OQ-canton-abroad)

acceptance_criteria.title: Only the 26 Swiss cantons can be chosen
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Switzerland is asked for the canton
acceptance_criteria.when: they choose it
acceptance_criteria.then: they choose one of the fund's 26 cantons: Aargau, Appenzell Ausserrhoden, Appenzell Innerrhoden, Basel-Landschaft, Basel-Stadt, Bern, Fribourg, Geneva, Glarus, Graubünden, Jura, Lucerne, Neuchâtel, Nidwalden, Obwalden, Schaffhausen, Schwyz, Solothurn, St. Gallen, Thurgau, Ticino, Uri, Valais, Vaud, Zug, Zurich

acceptance_criteria.title: Canton is dropped when the employee no longer lives in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee chose a canton and then changes the home address country to a country other than Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: they submit the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the canton is no longer asked and the earlier answer is not recorded; until submission it may be kept so that switching back loses no input

acceptance_criteria.title: Canton is recorded for the pension fund
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Switzerland has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: the answers are recorded
acceptance_criteria.then: the chosen canton is recorded for the pension fund's 'Canton' field

sections.title: First working day and insurance start date
sections.purpose: Ask the employee for the first working day and derive the pension fund insurance start date from it, so that the start date always falls on the 1st of a month and follows the latest first working day.

stories.title: Employee enters the first working day
stories.i_want: every new employee to state their first working day in the questionnaire, with the latest date always being the one that counts
stories.so_that: the pension fund registration has its most important input and a moved start date no longer goes unnoticed, as it did in Julia's case
stories.priority_reason: HR calls the first working day 'the number one thing' for the pension fund; a start date that was not updated caused a wrong insurance start, an unfriendly letter from the fund and weeks of fixing (Julia incident).

acceptance_criteria.title: First working day is always asked and required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee is filling in the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the employment step
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for their first working day as a date (DD.MM.YYYY); they cannot submit the questionnaire without it, whatever their other answers

examples.name: Any employee - first working day asked and required
Employee living abroad - first working day still asked and required

acceptance_criteria.title: First working day is recorded for the pension fund and HR
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered their first working day
acceptance_criteria.when: they submit the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the first working day is recorded for HR, which tracks the start date, and serves as the basis of the pension fund insurance start date (see US-02.2)

acceptance_criteria.title: The latest entered date counts while the employee is filling in the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered a first working day and then changes it before submitting, for example because they negotiated an earlier exit with their old employer
acceptance_criteria.when: they submit the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: only the latest first working day is recorded; no earlier date is kept

acceptance_criteria.title: After submission only HR changes the first working day
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: the first working day moves afterwards
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee cannot change it in the questionnaire any more; only HR can change it, the latest date replaces the earlier one without keeping a history, and the insurance start date follows the new date (see US-02.2). How HR makes the change is left to the later HR-side spec.

stories.title: Insurance start date derived from the first working day
stories.i_want: the insurance start date to be derived from the latest first working day and always to fall on the 1st of a month
stories.so_that: the employee is insured from the correct date and the fund is not given a wrong start date after the first working day has moved
stories.priority_reason: The fund requires an insurance start date on the 1st of a month; a start date that did not follow a moved first working day (Julia) led to a wrong registration and weeks of fixing.

acceptance_criteria.title: Employee is not asked for the insurance start date
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee is filling in the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they go through all steps
acceptance_criteria.then: they are never asked for an insurance start date; Lonio derives it from the first working day

acceptance_criteria.title: First working day on the 1st of a month
acceptance_criteria.given: the first working day is the 1st of a month
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the insurance start date
acceptance_criteria.then: insurance starts on the first working day itself

examples.name: Start on the 1st of a month

acceptance_criteria.given: the first working day is any day other than the 1st of a month
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the insurance start date
acceptance_criteria.then: insurance starts on the 1st of the following month, also across a year end

examples.name: Start on the 2nd of a month
Start at the end of the year

acceptance_criteria.title: Insurance start date follows every change of the first working day
acceptance_criteria.given: an insurance start date has been derived from a first working day
acceptance_criteria.when: the first working day changes, whether by the employee before submission or by HR after submission
acceptance_criteria.then: the insurance start date is derived again from the latest first working day; a start date based on an earlier first working day never remains

acceptance_criteria.title: Insurance start date is recorded for the pension fund
acceptance_criteria.given: the questionnaire has been submitted
acceptance_criteria.when: the insurance start date has been derived
acceptance_criteria.then: it is recorded for the pension fund's required 'Insurance start date' as DD.MM.YYYY and always falls on the 1st of a month

sections.title: Civil status and spouse for the pension fund
sections.purpose: Ask the civil status once. Map it to the fund's list and to married/single for source tax. Ask the spouse's or partner's date of birth only where the fund requires it.

stories.title: Ask the civil status once, using the pension fund's list
stories.i_want: to state my civil status once, choosing from a list that also covers registered partnership and separation
stories.so_that: both the pension fund and source tax get my civil status without being asked twice, and my real situation can be recorded
stories.priority_reason: Civil status is a required field of the pension fund registration; without it the registration is blocked. It also decides the source tax tariff.

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil status is asked of every employee and is required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee filling in the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the family step
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked their civil status, whatever their residence or nationality, and cannot submit the questionnaire without answering it

acceptance_criteria.title: Allowed civil status values
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is asked their civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: they choose an answer
acceptance_criteria.then: they can choose exactly one of: Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed, Registered partnership, Separated

acceptance_criteria.title: One answer serves both receiving parties
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered their civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire is submitted
acceptance_criteria.then: the answer is recorded once and is used both for the pension fund registration (see US-03.3) and for source tax (see US-03.4); the employee is not asked their civil status a second time

stories.title: Ask the spouse's date of birth from married employees
stories.i_want: the date of birth of the husband, wife or registered partner for every employee registered with me as Married
stories.so_that: the registration is not rejected for a missing spouse's date of birth

acceptance_criteria.title: Asked and required for Married, Registered partnership and Separated
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's civil status is Married, Registered partnership or Separated
acceptance_criteria.when: they fill in the family step
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked the date of birth of their husband, wife or registered partner, and must answer it

acceptance_criteria.title: Not asked for Single, Divorced or Widowed
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's civil status is Single, Divorced or Widowed
acceptance_criteria.when: they fill in the family step
acceptance_criteria.then: they are not asked a spouse's or partner's date of birth (whether the fund needs it for Divorced or Widowed is still open, see OQ-spouse-dob-other-status)

acceptance_criteria.title: Form of the answer and receiving party
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is asked the spouse's or partner's date of birth
acceptance_criteria.when: they answer
acceptance_criteria.then: the date is given as DD.MM.YYYY and is recorded for the pension fund registration, together with the civil status entered at the fund as Married

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's date of birth discarded when no longer applicable
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee entered a spouse's date of birth and then changed the civil status to Single, Divorced or Widowed
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire is submitted
acceptance_criteria.then: the spouse's date of birth is not recorded

stories.title: Enter the civil status in the pension fund's terms
stories.i_want: every employee's civil status expressed as one of my options (Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed)
stories.so_that: every new employee can be registered, including registered partners and separated employees, for whom my list has no option
stories.priority_reason: The fund's list lacks Registered partnership and Separated; without a mapping such employees (e.g. Daniel) cannot be registered.

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil statuses on the fund's list are taken over as they are
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee answered Single, Married, Divorced or Widowed
acceptance_criteria.when: the civil status for the pension fund is determined
acceptance_criteria.then: it is the same value as the employee's answer

acceptance_criteria.title: Registered partnership and Separated are provisionally entered as Married
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee answered Registered partnership or Separated
acceptance_criteria.when: the civil status for the pension fund is determined
acceptance_criteria.then: it is Married, provisionally until a domain expert and Pensionskasse Muster confirm how these employees are registered and whether the partner's details are wanted (see OQ-civil-status-partnership)

stories.title: Group the civil status for source tax
stories.i_want: the employee's civil status grouped into married (married or registered partnership) or single (single, divorced, separated, widowed), as the calculator does
stories.so_that: the spouse exemption and the tariff code are determined from the same civil status answer, without asking again
stories.priority_reason: Lonio now computes the tariff code itself (D-001); married vs single decides the tariff letter and whether the spouse exemption can apply.

acceptance_criteria.title: Married and registered partnership count as married
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee answered Married or Registered partnership
acceptance_criteria.when: the civil status for source tax is determined
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee counts as married for source tax, including for the spouse exemption

acceptance_criteria.title: Single, divorced, separated and widowed count as single
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee answered Single, Divorced, Separated or Widowed
acceptance_criteria.when: the civil status for source tax is determined
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee counts as single for source tax; a separated employee therefore gets no spouse exemption, even though the fund registers them as Married

sections.title: Source tax liability check
sections.purpose: Decide from residence, Swiss citizenship, C permit and the spouse exemption whether the employee is subject to source tax. Ask these facts only as far as they are needed, so that only employees subject to source tax get the source tax questions.

stories.title: Ask nationality and C permit only of employees living in Switzerland
stories.i_want: Lonio to ask employees living in Switzerland for their nationality and, if they are not Swiss, only whether they hold a C permit
stories.so_that: I know for each new employee whether they could be subject to source tax, without collecting nationality or permit data that no party needs
stories.priority_reason: HR today never knows up front who has to answer the source tax questions (F-hr_transcript-b84498); without these facts the source tax liability cannot be decided and the tariff code cannot be computed.

acceptance_criteria.title: Nationality is asked only of employees living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: the home address country is Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked for their nationality (countries by English name) and must answer it; employees living abroad are not asked, because they are subject to source tax whatever their nationality and get the permit reminder anyway. Whether the specific nationality or only 'Swiss citizen yes/no' is needed stays open (see OQ-nationality-scope).

acceptance_criteria.title: Swiss citizenship counts even with another nationality
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Switzerland holds Swiss citizenship, alone or together with another nationality
acceptance_criteria.when: they answer the nationality question
acceptance_criteria.then: they answer Switzerland, they count as Swiss and are not asked about a C permit

examples.name: Swiss (or dual Swiss) employee living in Switzerland

acceptance_criteria.title: Only 'C permit yes/no' is asked of non-Swiss employees living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland and is not Swiss
acceptance_criteria.when: they have answered the nationality question
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked whether they hold a C permit (permanent residence), answered yes or no, and must answer it; no other permit type is asked of anyone

acceptance_criteria.title: Who the answers are recorded for
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered nationality and, where asked, the C permit question
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire is submitted
acceptance_criteria.then: the answers are recorded for HR, for source tax (deciding whether the employee is subject to source tax) and, for nationality, for deciding whether the permit reminder is shown

stories.title: Ask spouse details only when the spouse could exempt the employee
stories.i_want: to be asked about my spouse or registered partner's residence, nationality and C permit only when these answers can change whether I am subject to source tax
stories.so_that: I give no personal data about my spouse that no party needs, while a Swiss or C-permit spouse living in Switzerland still exempts me from source tax
stories.priority_reason: Without the spouse details HR wrongly treats exempt employees like Tomás as subject to source tax; asking them of everyone would violate data minimisation (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's country of residence is asked only when the exemption can matter
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland, is not Swiss, holds no C permit and has given their civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: the civil status is Married or Registered partnership
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked in which country their spouse or registered partner lives (countries by English name) and must answer it; it is not asked of single, divorced, widowed or separated employees (separated counts as single for source tax), nor of employees who are Swiss, hold a C permit or live abroad. See OQ-nationality-scope on whether only 'lives in Switzerland yes/no' is needed.

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's nationality is asked only if the spouse lives in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee was asked where their spouse or registered partner lives
acceptance_criteria.when: the spouse lives in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked for the spouse's nationality (countries by English name; anyone with Swiss citizenship counts as Swiss) and must answer it; if the spouse lives abroad, neither the spouse's nationality nor C permit is asked

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's C permit is asked only if the spouse is not Swiss
acceptance_criteria.given: the spouse or registered partner lives in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the spouse is not Swiss
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether the spouse holds a C permit (permanent residence), answered yes or no, and must answer it; no other permit type is asked; for a Swiss spouse the question is not asked

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse exemption from source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's civil status and, where asked, the spouse's country of residence, nationality and C permit are known
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio checks the spouse exemption
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is exempted only if married or in a registered partnership with a spouse or partner who lives in Switzerland and is Swiss or holds a C permit; a spouse living abroad, a non-Swiss spouse without a C permit, and separated, single, divorced or widowed employees give no exemption

examples.name: Registered partner with C permit living in Switzerland

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse answers that no longer apply are not recorded
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered spouse questions and then changes an earlier answer (e.g. to holding a C permit, or to a civil status other than Married or Registered partnership) so that the spouse questions no longer apply
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire is submitted
acceptance_criteria.then: the earlier spouse answers are discarded and not recorded for any party; before submission they may be kept so that going back and forth loses no input

stories.title: Decide whether the employee is subject to source tax
stories.i_want: Lonio to decide from residence, Swiss citizenship, C permit and the spouse exemption whether a new employee is subject to source tax
stories.so_that: only employees subject to source tax get the source tax questions and a tariff result, and I no longer decide this by hand
stories.priority_reason: HR decides source tax liability by hand today and never knows up front who must answer the source tax questions (F-hr_transcript-b84498); the whole source tax step depends on this decision.

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees living abroad are always subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's home address country is not Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides source tax liability
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is subject to source tax whatever their nationality, even if Swiss; this includes residents of Liechtenstein, whose result then follows the Liechtenstein questions

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides source tax liability
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is not subject if Swiss (including dual nationals with Swiss citizenship), if holding a C permit, or if exempted by a Swiss or C-permit spouse or registered partner living in Switzerland; otherwise the employee is subject to source tax

examples.name: Single non-Swiss employee without C permit
Separated non-Swiss employee without C permit
Married, non-Swiss spouse without C permit

acceptance_criteria.title: Only employees subject to source tax get the source tax questions
acceptance_criteria.given: Lonio has decided whether the employee is subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the source tax step
acceptance_criteria.then: employees subject to source tax are asked the source tax questions (such as denomination); employees not subject are not asked them and get no source tax result

sections.title: Source tax tariff basics and computed result
sections.purpose: Ask the denomination and whether the spouse works. Combine these with the child digit and the cross-border outcome into the full Zurich tariff code (or the Liechtenstein result), which Lonio records for HR instead of HR using the calculator.

stories.title: State the denomination for the church-tax part of the tariff
stories.i_want: employees subject to source tax to state their denomination as one of the calculator's two groups
stories.so_that: the tariff code ends with the correct church-tax suffix (Y or N)
stories.priority_reason: Without the denomination no complete tariff code can be computed, and Lonio replaces HR's manual calculator step (D-001, F-hr_transcript-563a9f).

acceptance_criteria.title: Denomination is asked only from employees subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's answers so far show whether they are subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the source tax step
acceptance_criteria.then: the denomination is asked, and must be answered, only if the employee is subject to source tax; employees not subject to source tax are never asked. The answer is recorded for source tax (church-tax suffix).

examples.name: Non-Swiss without C permit living in Switzerland - subject
Swiss citizen living in Switzerland - not subject
C permit holder living in Switzerland - not subject

acceptance_criteria.title: Denomination offers the calculator's two groups

acceptance_criteria.when: they answer

acceptance_criteria.title: Denomination sets the church-tax suffix

acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio computes the tariff code
acceptance_criteria.then: the code ends with Y for 'Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed' and with N for 'None or other'.

stories.title: State whether the spouse or registered partner works, for married employees and registered partners
stories.i_want: married employees and registered partners subject to source tax to say whether their spouse or partner is gainfully employed or receives replacement income
stories.so_that: the married tariff letter is C or B as in the calculator
stories.priority_reason: Decides the tariff letter for every married employee subject to source tax; without it no tariff code can be computed (D-001, F-hr_transcript-09b3fe).

acceptance_criteria.title: Asked only from employees counting as married for source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the source tax step
acceptance_criteria.then: the question is asked, and must be answered yes or no, only if the employee is Married or in a Registered partnership; Single, Divorced, Widowed and Separated employees count as single for source tax and are not asked.
